liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Eyes of the World** (2 reviews): Reviewer hears the first Slipknot jam at the end of Eyes; Phil is in top form during Eyes [18][21]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer names Jack Straw among the tracks that set the standard for the period [11]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Tennessee Jed, usually a funny song, comes across as intense here [21]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China Cat into Rider transition is singled out as especially joyous [15]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Wharf Rat is cited alongside Brokedown Palace and China Cat into Rider as a standout of the era [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Bill Graham crew intro, Phil welcomes Mickey Hart**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-10-20.170419.aud.Conner.gems.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 30 songs; 255 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd74-10-20.sbd.finney.229.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 30 songs; 237 min; rated 4.19/5 by 21 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is very clean; reviewer wants some crowd noise and mentions an audience recording of some tracks that plays a full step fast; After Eyes of the World the sound changes, as if the taper moved; the mix is bass-heavy; Soundboard has occasional tinny moments [11][12][13][14][17][19]
- **gd1974-10-20.176674.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 31 songs; 239 min [4]
- **gd1974-10-20.sbd.smith-lee.GEMS.97193.flac16**: soundboard; 29 songs; 234 min; rated 3.64/5 by 14 [8]. Said about its sound: Sounds like a real-time multitrack mix with audience turned up between songs; Mississippi Half Step cuts in [8]

## Around the show

- Mickey Hart rejoined the band for this night, joked about as being sprung from a mental institution [15]
- Reviewer says the band melted what ice remained in the old skating rink [17]
- Band considered retiring, thinking this might be their last concert, as the Grateful Dead Movie recalls [21]
- Mickey Hart returns on drums and percussion for set 2 except Seastones, plus Sugar Magnolia and Johnny B. Goode [1]
- Reviewer rates this show above the 19th, which they also consider very good [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-10-20.170419.aud.Conner.gems.flac2496**: taped by Charles Conner; transferred by Transferred and mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Sony ECM-22P mic (mono) > Sony TC-55 > Maxell UD C-90 cassettes [1]. Also: First known master audience source for this date, from Charles Conner's master cassettes; another uncirculated audience source patches gaps [1]
- **gd74-10-20.sbd.finney.229.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Mixed sources via D. Finney, stemming from the Frank's Picks tree; info file lists flaws [3]
- **gd1974-10-20.176674.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Louis Falanga; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Louis Falanga's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM 250 mic > Sony TC-110 (Maxell UD C120) [4]. Also: Sony ECM 22p source from Charles Connor supplies short patches, including Tennessee Jed, China Cat, Seastones and Eyes of the World [4]
- **gd1974-10-20.sbd.smith-lee.GEMS.97193.flac16**: transferred by Matt Smith and Jamie Waddell; source: Multitrack MR>2 track mixdown>?R>R>CD [8]. Also: Transfer by Matt Smith from Pat Lee's tapes; Winterland '74 reels are black Maxell UDII at 3 3/4 ips [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Winterland Arena - October 20, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/october-20-1974) [23]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Winterland Arena - October 20, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/october-20-1974) [24]
